Rohachiv Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Zhytomyr Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. Rohachiv's cemetery, established in the 19th century, was also used by the Jewish community of nearby Kamianyi Brid, documented elsewhere in this collection, until 1919. Rohachiv's own Jewish population reached an extraordinary 94 percent of the town by 1897. In 1920, about 30 Jews were killed in a pogrom carried out by Red Army soldiers — one of several such rare attributions recorded across this cluster of towns, alongside Baranivka and Lyubar, both documented elsewhere in this collection. Most of Rohachiv's remaining Jews were murdered on Yom Kippur, October 1, 1941. An older, disused Jewish cemetery is also known to have existed in the town center as early as the 1890s, though it is not otherwise documented here.
